### Get the data that will be used for itols

```{r}

## Tree created with the single-copy core genes from the 117 AVT strains
tree<-read.tree(here("Genotype", "Data_input", "AVT_single_copy_core_concat.fasta.treefile")) 
tree

## Extract the strains in the tree which represents what Sohini used in Guha et al., 2026

tip_strains <- data.frame(Strain_Code = tree$tip.label) #I am using the Strain_Code name to match the column name for that type of naming system in Strains_Description_Phenotype_Github.xlsx

## Add the information I am interested in, particularly Morphology 

Strains <- read_excel(here("Genotype", "Data_input", "Strains_Description_Phenotype_Github.xlsx"))
Strains ## I will use Morphology and Pairs
```

## SNP differences between pairs

```{r}

## This tables was obtained with the code bcftools gtcheck  -u GT,GT strain_118_variants_diploid.vcf according to Guha et al., (2026)

mismatch_data <- read_lines(here("Genotype", "Data_input", "strain_118_variants_pairwise_mismatches.tsv"))

# Keep only the actual data rows (they start with "DCv2")
data_lines <- mismatch_data[startsWith(mismatch_data, "DCv2")]

gtcheck_data <- read_tsv(
  I(data_lines),   # I() tells read_tsv to treat this as literal text, not a filepath
  col_names = c("Tag", "Query_Sample", "Genotyped_Sample", "Discordance",
                "Avg_neg_log_P_HWE", "Sites_compared", "Matching_genotypes")
)

gtcheck_data <- gtcheck_data %>% dplyr::select(-Tag)

### Not all of the genotypes that have been compared are pairs, so I am going to only filter for the ones that are paired: 

Pairs <- read_excel(here("Genotype", "Data_input", "Strains_Description_Phenotype_Github.xlsx"))
#View(Pairs)
Pairs <- Pairs %>% filter(!is.na(Pairs))

pairs_wide <- Pairs %>%
  dplyr::select(Strain_Code, Morphology, Pairs) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Morphology, values_from = Strain_Code)
#View(pairs_wide)

### I am not interested in which is the query_sample and which one is the genotyped_sample in the strain_118_variants_pairwise_mismatches.tsv. Therefore I will reorganize the gtcheck_data accordingly:

### Sort the two strain names alphabetically first, so the same pair always produces the same key regardless of which strain in gtcheck is query or genotyped

pairs_wide <- pairs_wide %>%
  rowwise() %>% ## rowwise() always goes paired with ungroup(). rowwise() function converts a dataframe into a special grouped form where every single row is treated as its own individual group
  mutate(pair_key = paste(sort(c(Mucoid, Dry)), collapse = "_")) %>%
  ungroup()
pairs_wide

gtcheck_data <- gtcheck_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(pair_key = paste(sort(c(Query_Sample, Genotyped_Sample)), collapse = "_")) %>%
  ungroup() ## The idea is to put the two strains names in the same alphabetical order no matter which one came first. So it will create an identical key of AVT29_AVT98 than the one created in pairs_wide

#View(gtcheck_data)


mismatch_filtered <- merge(pairs_wide, gtcheck_data, by = "pair_key")

## I want to calculate the number of SNP differences 

mismatch_filtered <- mismatch_filtered %>%
  mutate(SNP_differences = Sites_compared - Matching_genotypes)
#View(mismatch_filtered)

mismatch_filtered


hist(mismatch_filtered$SNP_differences)



## For itols I will only extract the mismatches and pairs
mismatch_filtered
mismatch_filtered_subset <- mismatch_filtered %>% dplyr::select(c("Pairs", "Mucoid", "Dry", "SNP_differences"))
mismatch_filtered_subset

SNPs_Pairs <- pivot_longer(mismatch_filtered_subset,
              cols = c(Mucoid, Dry),
             names_to = "Morphology",
             values_to = "Strains")

SNPs_Pairs

SNPs_Pair_wide <- SNPs_Pairs %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Morphology,
              values_from = Strains)
SNPs_Pair_wide
SNPs_Pair_wide <- SNPs_Pair_wide %>% dplyr::rename("Mucoid strain" = "Mucoid", 
                                            "Dry strain" = "Dry") %>%  dplyr::select(c("Pairs", "Mucoid strain", "Dry strain", "SNP_differences"))

SNPs_Pair_wide

### This file is not using the way I name them, it is using the way they were labeled in Guha et al., 2026. 

write_xlsx(SNPs_Pair_wide, here("Genotype", "Tables", "EPS_TableS6_FromR.xlsx"))


```
Test for phylogenetic independence 

```{r}

# Testing independent origins of the dry phenotype

#I will use phylo.d (caper). tests whether the dry/mucoid phenotype is phylogenetically clumped (D=0, one ancestral origin retained by descent) or randomly scattered across tips (D=1, consistent with independent/convergent origins).


# Root the FULL tree (117 strains + 2 outgroup strains) using the outgroups 

full_tree <- read.tree(here("Genotype", "Data_input", "AVT_single_copy_core_concat_outgroup.fasta.treefile"))
full_tree #I am including the file that has three outgroups

#full_tree$tip.label

### From the .Rmd in Guha et al., 2026 I found 

full_tree$tip.label[full_tree$tip.label == "AVT7827695.1"] <- "Sinorhizobium medicae USDA1037"
full_tree$tip.label[full_tree$tip.label == "AVT6965.1"]    <- "Sinorhizobium meliloti RM1021"
full_tree$tip.label[full_tree$tip.label == "AVT2197065.1"] <- "Sinorhizobium meliloti USDA1106"

full_tree     

tree2 <- drop.tip(full_tree, "Sinorhizobium medicae USDA1037")
tree_rooted2 <- root(
  tree2,
  outgroup = c("Sinorhizobium meliloti RM1021",
               "Sinorhizobium meliloti USDA1106"),
  resolve.root = TRUE
)

# Then I will drop the outgroups, since I have no complete phenotype data for them

analysis_tree <- drop.tip(tree_rooted2, c("Sinorhizobium meliloti RM1021", "Sinorhizobium meliloti USDA1106"))
analysis_tree


# Resolve any polytomies on the now-pruned, rooted tree. I don't think the tree had a polytomies now that I am taking a second look at it, so I don't think this was needed in the analysis, but this should not change the result. Consider pruning this step after reviewing.
analysis_tree <- multi2di(analysis_tree)
analysis_tree
analysis_tree$edge.length[analysis_tree$edge.length == 0] <- 1e-8


### I will create a dataframe that will also be used to run the GWAS with binary traits using pyseer

Strains_pyseer <- Strains %>% mutate(Binary_trait = ifelse(Morphology == "Mucoid", 1,0))
Strains_pyseer <- Strains_pyseer %>% dplyr::select(c("Strain_Code", "Binary_trait"))
Strains_pyseer <- Strains_pyseer %>% rename("samples" = "Strain_Code") ## pyseer wants it labeled as "samples".
Strains_pyseer


###
pheno <- Strains_pyseer
pheno

matched <- treedata(analysis_tree, setNames(pheno[["Binary_trait"]], pheno[["samples"]]),
                     sort = TRUE, warnings = TRUE)
analysis_tree <- matched$phy
analysis_tree

pheno_vec <- matched$data[, 1]  # named character vector "Dry"/"Mucoid"
pheno_vec

cat("Tree has", Ntip(tree), "tips after matching.\n")
cat("Phenotype counts:\n")
print(table(pheno_vec)) #Yes, this has the right information


# phylo.d: is the phenotype clumped or scattered on the tree?

# phylo.d needs a data.frame (not just a vector) with a binary 0/1 column, plus a comparative.data object linking that data.frame to the tree.

pheno_df <- data.frame(
  strain = names(pheno_vec),
  dry_binary = pheno_vec
)

pheno_df ## Mucoid is 1 and dry is 0

#View(pheno_df)

set.seed(123) ### My results changed slightly from what I currently have in the manuscript because I did not set.seed before, but nothing that changes the interpretation

is.rooted(analysis_tree)
is.binary(analysis_tree)


comp_data <- comparative.data(
  phy       = analysis_tree,       # fixed
  data      = pheno_df,
  names.col = "strain",
  vcv       = FALSE                # phylo.d doesn't need it
)

comp_data

d_result <- phylo.d(
  data = comp_data,
  binvar = dry_binary,
  permut = 1000
)

print(d_result)


d_summary <- data.frame(
  N_tips = length(comp_data$phy$tip.label),
  D_estimate = d_result$DEstimate,
  P_random_D1 = d_result$Pval1,
  P_brownian_D0 = d_result$Pval0,
  Permutations = 1000   # the number you set, not d_result$Permutations
                         # (that field holds the 1000 simulated null D values,
                         # not a count -- hardcode the number you specified)
)

print(d_summary)

write_csv(d_summary, here("Genotype", "Tables", "EPS_TableS4_FromR.csv"))



```

## Genotypic data: presence absence ##

This will have the presence absence and the SNP data

```{r}

#### presence/absence matrix ####

# I will work with the .Rtab from the panaroo outcome. I will extract the .Rtab file from the following path: /storage/home/mag6678/burghardt/Kayla/avtPacBio/panaroo_output and import them to my local computer

gene_presence_absence_pyseer <- read.delim(here("Genotype", "Data_input", "gene_presence_absence.Rtab"), header = TRUE) #I opened panaroo output. In this file strains were labeled in a different way than they were labeled in the phylogenetic tree in Guha et al., 2026, so in the next steps I homogenized the labeling system 
gene_presence_absence_pyseer
gene_presence_absence_pyseer <- gene_presence_absence_pyseer %>% dplyr::select(-c("strain_NIG", "strain_EXC")) #Remove the strains that are not part of the AVT collection.

Strains <- read_excel(here("Genotype", "Data_input", "Strains_Description_Phenotype_Github.xlsx")) # Import the table with the AVT format labels used in Guha et al., 2026 (Strain_Code) and the the one used in this manuscript (Strain). I want the codes in these R.tab document to have the same format than Strain_Code

Strains_panaroo <- Strains %>% mutate(Strain_panaroo = paste0("strain_", Strain)) # Replicate the labeling system used in Panaroo
Strains_panaroo

## Replace the names in the gene_presence_absence_edited with the AVT1, AVT2, AVT3 names: build the rename map: names(new) = old column name, values = new column name
rename_map <- setNames(Strains_panaroo$Strain_panaroo, Strains_panaroo$Strain_Code) 
gene_presence_absence_pyseer <- gene_presence_absence_pyseer %>% rename(any_of(rename_map))
gene_presence_absence_pyseer

#write_tsv(gene_presence_absence_pyseer, here("Genotype", "Tables", "gene_presence_absence_rtab_pyseer.tsv"))

## Cut the genes that are present in less than 5% and therefore also more than 95% of the strain collection

strain_cols <- names(gene_presence_absence_pyseer)[-1]
strain_cols

nrow(gene_presence_absence_pyseer) #12591 groups

gene_pa_filtered <- gene_presence_absence_pyseer %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(af = mean(c_across(all_of(strain_cols)))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(af >= 0.05 & af <= 0.95) %>%
  dplyr::select(-af) ## By cutting the genes that were present in more than 100% I am cutting the genes that were present in all of the strains, which is good because I do not want to work with genes that were invariant.

gene_pa_filtered

nrow(gene_pa_filtered) # 3760

write_tsv(gene_pa_filtered, here("Genotype", "Tables",  "gene_presence_absence_rtab_pyseer_maf05.tsv")) 

```

## Genotypic data: SNPs ##

This code was run in the batch 

```{r, eval=FALSE}


### Filter the vcf file 

vcftools --vcf strain_118_variants.vcf \
  --minQ 20 --maf 0.05 --max-missing 0.8 \
  --recode --out strain_118_filtered
# This step created strain_118_filtered.log which displays information about the filtering step, and strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf, which is the vcf file after the filtering step. 

### To enable rapid regional querying, we used bgzip to sort genomic coordinates and compress them, and tabix, to generate spatial indexes. 

bgzip strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf ## Creates the document strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz

tabix -p vcf strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz ##strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz.tbi


```

### RUN PYSEER

This was done in the terminal 

Account for population structure

```{r, eval = FALSE}

### Turn the tree in a similarity matrix using pyseer helper script that can be obtained in pyseer github repository (https://github.com/mgalardini/pyseer). It is currently in this path: /storage/home/mag6678/burghardt/MariaGil/pyseer. I will use the script phylogeny_distance.py  to create the kinship matrix that will be used as a random effect when I run pyseer. I will also create the phylogeny_distance_forglm.tsv, that is a distance matrix that for the glm() where the trait is binary. I am using the file that does not have the outgroups

# I will use a glm() when working with the binary phenotype mucoid and dry. I used the script phylogeny_distance.py (do not use the flag -lmm)

python /storage/home/mag6678/burghardt/MariaGil/pyseer/scripts/phylogeny_distance.py /storage/home/mag6678/burghardt/MariaGil/EPS_genes/panaroo/tree/AVT_single_copy_core_concat.fasta.treefile > phylogeny_distance_forglm.tsv

# I will use lmm() when working with the glucose continuous phenotype (-lmm) to construct the kinship matrix

python /storage/home/mag6678/burghardt/MariaGil/pyseer/scripts/phylogeny_distance.py --lmm /storage/home/mag6678/burghardt/MariaGil/EPS_genes/panaroo/tree/AVT_single_copy_core_concat.fasta.treefile > phylogeny_similarity.tsv

```

# Script to run pyseer #

```{r, eval=FALSE}

conda install bioconda::pyseer

#### Presence absence (PA)  ####
#### I think after the review I might need to standardize the names of the pyseer files


### Pyseer code to run the presence absence data using the binary phenotype where Mucoid is 1 and Dry is 0.

pyseer --phenotypes Data_input/Binary_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --pres Data_input/gene_presence_absence_rtab_pyseer_maf05.tsv \
  --distances Data_input/phylogeny_distance_forglm.tsv \
  --max-dimensions 8 \
  --output-patterns patterns_glm_binary_PA.txt \
  > pyseer_results_glm_binary_PA.txt



### Pyseer code to run the presence absence data using the continuous anthrone values where each phenotypic value is the Glucose/OD600

pyseer --lmm --phenotypes Data_input/Glucose_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --pres Data_input/gene_presence_absence_rtab_pyseer_maf05.tsv \
  --similarity Data_input/phylogeny_similarity.tsv \
  --output-patterns patterns_Glucose_maf05_PA.txt \
  > pyseer_results_Glucose_maf05_PA.txt
# h^2 = 0.50




#### SNPs ####

In the binary phenotype we ran a generalized linear model where the population structure was accounted based on the distances stated by the phylogenetic tree

pyseer --phenotypes Data_input/Binary_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --vcf Data_input/strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz \
  --distances Data_input/phylogeny_distance_forglm.tsv \
  --max-dimensions 8 \
  --output-patterns patterns_glm_binary_snps.txt \
  > pyseer_results_glm_binary_snps.txt


In the glucose phenotype the population structure was accounted as the kinship matrix 

pyseer --lmm --phenotypes Data_input/Glucose_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --vcf Data_input/strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz \
  --similarity Data_input/phylogeny_similarity.tsv \
  --output-patterns patterns_snps_glucose.txt \
  > pyseer_snp_results_glucose.txt

#h^2 = 0.50


To calculate the number of genes/SNP variants that covary across all of the strains I used the count_patterns.py that is part of the pyseer github folder. 



```
